sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A perennial of European beaches, dunes and sandy shores. Its leathery rosette and 15–60 cm stems are glaucous and spiny; a taproot anchors it in sand.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: Flowers are grouped in heads surrounded by spiny bracts and are often pale blue. The fruit is dry and splits into two mericarps; it is not a berry.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: The sources consulted describe mainly historical non-food uses and do not establish safe consumption.
